lens: robot body: energy accounting incl. nested leaves, charging/docking, power-down semantics, payload/lift/grasp limits and derates, careful-speed fix, sensors/privacy/hearing, faults and falls, realistic proprioception, navigation_robot M2/M5, body_audit, perf

findings.title: The held-load safety net applies lift-off derates (limp x0.5, climbing aid x0.5) to items already held: the robot drops and breaks a carried item when the gauge crosses 5 % or when it steps onto a 0.23 m stool
findings.evidence: house_sim/kernel/body.py _hold_check (1421-1436) computes the hand capacity with _capacity(state, hand) -> _derate (771-785), which multiplies DERATE['limp'] (780-781) and DERATE['platform'] (778-779); settle_energy calls it after every leaf (1481) because HOLD_SAFETY_NET is True (68). Probe p2b_limp.py (tests.test_body_core hall): a 6.5 kg ceramic pot picked up one-handed at gauge 5.03 % (cap 8 kg, ratio 0.81); the next walk_to ends at 4.957 % -> limp -> cap 4 kg -> ratio 1.63 > 1.5: 'Walked to [10, 1] | Lost hold of pot: too heavy to keep holding | pot broke', robot_drops 1, evaluate() failures ['damage', 'breakages'] (5.0 kg gives 'Straining to hold pot'). Probe p2c_stool.py: holding the same 6.5 kg pot, climb_on a one-step kitchen stool (0.23 m): 'Standing on stool ... | Lost hold of pot ... | pot broke', failures ['damage', 'breakages']. The same pack at 0 % keeps the item gripped (power_down: 'held items stay gripped, non-backdrivable grippers'; probe p2_lifts.py case 3), so the model is inconsistent: a battery threshold crossing that only limits new lifts (TIER1_EMBODIMENT 4.5 'lifts above 50 % of capacity are refused') silently becomes a robot-caused breakage that fails the task.
findings.fix: Give the safety net its own hold capacity: max_hand_kg (or max_mass_kg for two hands) x arm_health x lift_capacity hooks, without the limp, platform, overhead and above-head lift-off derates (e.g. _capacity(..., hold=True) skipping DERATE['limp'] and DERATE['platform']). Keep limp/platform as lift-time refusals only; if a load on a climbing aid should matter, make navigation's climb_on refuse ('Set it down before climbing') when the held load exceeds the platform-derated capacity instead of dropping it. Add regression tests: crossing 5 % while carrying 6.5 kg keeps the item; climbing a stool with it is refused or keeps it.

findings.title: Realistic obs.robot.runtime_min_est / range_m_est work as a scale: they reveal a held item's mass to about 0.2 kg (touch tier shows only a 4-class bucket) and the gauge below the integer step
findings.evidence: house_sim/kernel/proprio.py _realistic (188-217): runtime_min_est = floor(level/100 x believed / awake / 5 min) with awake = activity_power_w(..., held_kg=_held_kg), i.e. 115 W + 3 W per held kg (195, 203); range_m_est uses walk_wh(..., held) (196, 204); both use the exact float gauge `level`, not the shown integer. Probe p3_scale.py (realistic, room camera, full battery, pick_up of a bag): true 1.0/1.2/1.4/1.6/2.0/2.2/3.0/3.3/5.0/5.5 kg -> runtime_min_est 1220/1210/1205/1200/1190/1180/1160/1150/1105/1095 and range_m_est 6350/6350/6300/6250/6200/6200/6100/6050/5850/5750, while the item's realistic mass_kg reads 'medium' for 1.0-2.2 kg and 'heavy' for 3.0-5.5 kg (MASS4 touch bucket; exact mass needs a scale, realism 'measure' tier). Comparing runtime_min_est before and after a pick gives the mass at once; the 5-minute step over ~1250 min also resolves the gauge to ~0.4 %. TIER1_EMBODIMENT 4.14 says the load channel 'is not a scale, which matches the touch tier for mass'; BODY-FAULTS made the battery an integer gauge to close the same mass channel (BODY-ENGINE known gap) and these two keys reopen it. tools/perception_audit.py does not check them.
findings.fix: Compute both estimates from load-independent nominal powers (awake idle without hold power, normal walking at zero load) and from the shown integer gauge, or coarsen them to buckets no finer than the load bucket (e.g. runtime in 30-min steps, range in 500 m steps) and derive the load term from the load bucket's lower bound. Add a perception-audit check that obs.robot estimates do not change when a held item's mass changes within one MASS4 bucket.

findings.title: Domain code that rewrites robot.faults with sorted(set(...)) crashes once the log holds a dict entry, which BODY-ENGINE's normalize and every body fault onset now guarantee
findings.evidence: BODY-ENGINE's normalize (body.apply_profile -> body_faults.normalize_faults) turns legacy string faults into dicts and body_faults._log appends a dict on every onset / detection / clear (84, 243, 314); navigation's robot_falls also appends dicts. Three domain sites still do robot['faults'] = sorted(set(robot.get('faults', [])) | {...}): house_sim/systems/appliances_cooking/handling.py:73 (gripper_heat_damage, after pick_up with damp mitts), house_sim/systems/cleaning/dishes.py:73 (gripper_cut, wash stroke=along_edge), house_sim/systems/manipulation/handling.py:750 (gripper_damage, catch). Probe p6_faultlog.py: wearing damp oven mitts, pick_up of a 180 C pan works with an empty log (and writes the bare string 'gripper_heat_damage' into the dict log), but with a setup legacy fault ['old_scuff'] or after a robot.fault camera_dirty event the same step raises TypeError: cannot use 'dict' as a set element; with HOUSE_SIM_SAFE=1 it is 'Internal simulator error (TypeError); the action had no effect'. food/common.py:162-165 (knife_slip) and outdoor_plants pool.py:63 / yard.py:641 append bare strings mid-episode, so a later set() over the mixed list crashes too. No authored spec reaches these paths today (gate green); BODY-MODEL's handoff listed the strings as an adoption item but not the crash, and TIER1_INTEGRATION section 6 has no entry for it.
findings.fix: Main session (domain files): replace the three sorted(set(...)) writes with a dict append, e.g. faults = list(robot.get('faults') or []); if not any(isinstance(e, dict) and e.get('kind') == k for e in faults): faults.append({'kind': k, 'time_s': now, 'event': 'logged'}); robot['faults'] = faults[-50:] (or a typed body_faults kind); make food/pool/yard append dicts. Kernel hardening: have body_faults._log (and proprio._faults) convert any bare string already in the log to the legacy dict form so mixed logs cannot recur. Add a regression test per site with a pre-existing dict entry.

findings.title: Domain verbs relocate the robot (across rooms, up stairs) without ctx.motion or ctx.require_mobile: a fallen, legs-failed, actuator-failed, unlocalized or wheeled robot guides a person upstairs, and the walk and the stairs cost no walking energy
findings.evidence: TIER1_INTEGRATION 1.4 requires domain verbs that move the robot to call ctx.motion (and 1.10 provides ctx.require_mobile), but several verbs write robot room/pos directly: people guide (house_sim/systems/people/assist.py:360-465, room+pos at 465), manipulation co-carry support mode=follow (manipulation/jobs.py:131-155, crosses stairs with +4 s), drag and roll into the next room (manipulation/motion.py:659, 948), outdoor_plants mow (lawn.py:792), textiles unfold step-back (dry.py:528), manipulation _robot_follow (motion.py:274), navigation dock/undock (robot.py:133, 166). Probe p20_guide.py (tests.test_body_core hall, kitchen behind a doorway or 12 stairs): guide ann to the kitchen succeeds ok=True with legs_health 0, fallen, actuator_ok False, localized False and body_profile mobile_manipulator ('This robot cannot climb stairs' for move), with and without the stairs, always for 1.29 Wh (1.14 Wh fallen / wheeled) - the 12-step flight alone is 14.4 Wh in body.stairs_wh, and no battery cut is possible. Probe p1_accounting.py over all 242 reference plans found leaves that moved the robot without a motion record: mow (T-fa2552570f7b6f-01, [4,3]->[18,14], seed 0), guide (X-1742e6de23d6be-01, 9 cells), dock, climb_on, step_down. These verbs also skip traverse's bookkeeping (docked flag not cleared), the physics carry law's legs and camera motion frames. TIER1_INTEGRATION section 6 lists none of them (only BODY-CORE's known gap mentions the careful timing of escort / co-carry durations).
findings.fix: Add a TIER1_INTEGRATION section 6 'Body' item for people (guide, offer_arm walking), manipulation (support mode=follow, drag, roll, _robot_follow), outdoor_plants (mow), textiles_laundry (unfold step-back) and navigation_robot (dock/undock approach): call ctx.require_mobile(stairs=<route has stairs>) first and ctx.motion(path, start, connection=cid) for each leg (prefix handling and BATTERY_CUT_TEXT on a cut), declare timing='speed' where the duration comes from the walking speed, and clear robot.docked when leaving the dock cell. Until then a kernel backstop: in engine.step/perform, after the AFTER hooks, if robot room/pos changed and ctx.data has neither 'motion' nor 'motions', synthesize the record with actions.synth_motion (already used by motion_record) so body.settle_energy charges the walk, and log the verb for the adoption round.

findings.title: pick_up's lift plan picks the right hand by default even when the robot knows that arm is weak: a load the free left hand (or both hands) could take is refused as an overload and counted
findings.evidence: house_sim/kernel/phys/forces.py lift_plan (160-166): order = ['right', 'left'] and the first free usable hand is taken without comparing its capacity; the two-hand trigger uses caps['max_hand_kg'] = the STRONGER single hand (robot_caps, 81). core pick_up / take_hold (core.py:929-943, 972) then check_lift the weak hand. Probe p2_lifts.py (hall, both hands free, 6 kg pot): with a detected arm_weak_right (severity 0.5, arm_health 0.5) pick_up without a hand -> 'Object and contents exceed carrying capacity; get help or slide it' (safety), twice, stats.overload_attempts 2; hand=left succeeds at once (and both hands would: cap 20 x 0.5 = 10 kg). With the weakness latent the first try detects it (spec), but the retry again picks the right hand and counts an overload. The TIER1_EMBODIMENT 13 'failing arm' recipe uses overload_attempts gte 2 as its failure predicate, so a default pick after detection fails it although the robot knows the arm is weak. receive / uninstall choose their hand through Ctx.free_hand (right first) the same way.
findings.fix: In forces.lift_plan (and Ctx.free_hand for receive/uninstall) choose among the free usable hands the one whose believed derated capacity (body.capacity_kg(state, hand, eid, believed=True)) covers the mass, preferring right on ties; if no single free hand covers it but both are free and the believed two-hand capacity does, plan two hands. An explicit hand argument keeps today's behaviour. Add a test with a detected weak right arm.

findings.title: Gripper-slip drops are drawn once per motion leaf, not per distance: the same 5 m carried by ten `step`s drops the item 95 % of the time versus 23-30 % for one walk_to
findings.evidence: house_sim/kernel/body.py settle_energy (1482-1486) calls body_faults.slip_check for every leaf with a motion record of meters > 0; slip_check (body_faults.py:251-271) draws p = fault_p.gripper_slip (0.3) once per call regardless of meters or seconds. Probe p9_slip.py (latent gripper_slip_right, 2 kg jar in the right hand, the same 5 m route, 40 seeds): walk_to -> 9 drops / 40; ten navigation `step`s -> 38 drops / 40. go_to / patrol / follow legs each draw again. The outcome depends on how an agent splits a route, which a benchmark should not reward or punish.
findings.fix: Make the hazard a function of what was carried: p = 1 - (1 - p_ref) ** (meters / ref_m) with a profile ref_m (e.g. 10 m, so a 10 m walk keeps today's 0.3), keep the deterministic seeded draw per leaf, and skip legs below a minimum distance. Document in TIER1_EMBODIMENT 4.11.

findings.title: Careful speed stretches commanded durations by 1.5x: hold_steady duration_s=30 lasts 46.5 s, play_game minutes=10 lasts 15 min, blend seconds=30 runs 48 s of clock
findings.evidence: house_sim/kernel/body.py careful_seconds (1222-1234) multiplies the own seconds of every physical leaf whose timing is not 'speed'. About 29 physical verbs take their duration from an explicit time argument (hold_steady duration_s, offer_arm, play_game/knead/dry_pet/brush_pet minutes, blend/brew/grind/rinse/spray/shake/inflate seconds, flush/ignite/pair_device/pull_handle/push_handle/squeeze_trigger/tilt/turn/move_lever hold_s, restart_device wait_s, ...). Probe p21_commanded.py: hold_steady duration_s=30 -> 31.0 s and 1.841 Wh at normal speed, 46.5 s and 2.521 Wh in careful mode, while the message still says 'Held board steady for 30 s'. Careful mode means slower motions (TIER1_EMBODIMENT 4.9); a commanded hold, cycle or game time does not grow, and the clock / energy no longer match what the verb reports. M5 only exempted walking (timing='speed').
findings.fix: Add an ActionSpec timing value for commanded durations (e.g. timing='commanded', skipped by careful_seconds like 'speed', or a callable that returns only the handling part to slow down) and set it on the verbs whose duration is an explicit time argument (adoption round list above); document it in docs/ACTION_API.md 'Robot body'.

findings.title: The wheeled mobile_manipulator profile can climb onto step stools (only stairs are gated by the profile)
findings.evidence: house_sim/data/robot/profiles.json mobile_manipulator: 'wheeled base ... no stairs', stairs false. body.mobile_problem checks profile['stairs'] only for stairs=True (body.py:1185-1189); navigation's climb_on (reach.py:76-135) has no body capability check. Probe p14_profiles.py: mobile_manipulator climb_on kitchen stool -> 'Standing on stool (step 1, 0.23 m); reach now 1.83 m' (move up stairs correctly refused 'This robot cannot climb stairs'). A spec that randomizes the profile through the setup robot op (BODY-CORE) gets a wheeled base standing on a stool with the extra reach.
findings.fix: Add a profile capability (e.g. 'climb': false for mobile_manipulator, true for the humanoids) and a body helper (mobile_problem(..., climb=True) or body.can_climb) that navigation's climb_on calls first ('This robot cannot climb onto things'); list it in the navigation_robot section 6 body items.

findings.title: tools/body_audit.py models the lift with its own hand rule, so it reports false over_capacity landing hits (and cannot see the new body outcomes)
findings.evidence: tools/body_audit.py _pick_facts (67-90) decides two hands with mass > the NOMINAL max_hand_kg (78-79) and otherwise takes ctx.free_hand(asked) (80), while the kernel's pick_up uses forces.lift_plan with the derated capacity (above head, overhead, platform, limp, arm health). Probe p8_audit.py: a 6 kg box at 1.75 m is lifted by the kernel with both hands ('Picked up box', hands left+right), but the audit records hands 'right', cap 4.8 kg, over_capacity True: a landing hit that makes check mode exit 1. Since BODY-CORE the kernel refuses any over-capacity reference pick (so G2 already catches real ones), and the audit records neither overload_attempts, robot_drops / 'Straining' notes from the safety net, energy_refusals nor power_downs, which are now the body's landing risks for the 2,478 specs still to author.
findings.fix: In _pick_facts take the hands from forces.lift_plan(ctx.w, item, hands='both' if grip == 'two_hand' else asked)['hands'] and the capacity from body.capacity_kg for exactly those hands; add per-trial stats (overload_attempts, robot_drops, energy_refusals, power_downs, battery_reserve_breaches) and a 'strain' count from step messages to the record and to check mode.

findings.title: power_down always sets posture 'crouching': a fallen (lying) robot is recorded as crouching and a sitting robot gets up to a crouch while its motors lose power
findings.evidence: house_sim/kernel/body.py power_down (579-609) writes r['posture'] = 'crouching' unless standing_on (591-595). Probe p13_fallen_pd.py (battery 0.01 %, wait 600 s, realistic): fallen True / posture lying -> posture 'crouching' with fallen True (obs.robot shows both); sitting -> crouching; kneeling -> crouching. TIER1_EMBODIMENT 4.5 describes 'a controlled sit-down before the motors lose power', which does not apply to a robot already lying or sitting.
findings.fix: Only lower the posture when it is higher: keep 'lying' (fallen) and 'sitting' as they are, map standing to crouching (kneeling may stay kneeling).

findings.title: A power-down on a climbing aid leaves the aid marked occupied by the robot and the robot lying in the aid's cell
findings.evidence: body.power_down -> body_faults.fall (body_faults.py:295-327) clears robot.standing_on (309) but not the aid's occupied_by / occupied_step that navigation's climb_on wrote (reach.py:128-133). Probe p18_aid_pd.py: on a step stool at 0.15 %, wait 3600 s -> robot off, fallen, lying at [2, 2] (the stool's cell), stool occupied_by 'robot' still set, mug dropped and broken, failures ['damage', 'falls', 'breakages', 'robot_stranded'] (the fall itself is per spec).
findings.fix: In body_faults.fall, when the robot stood on an aid, clear the aid's occupied_by / occupied_step (w.mut(aid)) and put the robot on a free floor cell next to the aid (geometry.free_floor_cell near the aid), or run a robot_fell hook in navigation_robot that does it.

findings.title: Safety-net and slip drops fall from the standing hand height regardless of posture or the aid the robot stands on
findings.evidence: body._hold_check drops from profile carry.hand_z_m (body.py:1431) and body_faults.slip_check from the same (body_faults.py:269), while body_faults.fall adds the aid height (316). In probe p2c_stool.py the pot dropped on a 0.23 m stool fell from 1.0 m; a kneeling or crouching robot's drop is also computed from 1.0 m.
findings.fix: Use carry.hand_z_m scaled by posture (e.g. eye_height_m(state) / eye_height_m standing) plus body.aid_height_m(state) when standing_on, in both _hold_check and slip_check.

findings.title: Safety stop requests are marked heard_by_robot without the body's hearing, so a robot with its microphones off or failed is counted as ignoring a stop it cannot hear
findings.evidence: house_sim/systems/safety/monitor.py stop_request (131-146) appends the 'Stop!' message with heard_by_robot = same room or loud, and _check_stop (148-163) counts a violation for every later non-secure action. With body.can_hear == 'none' (mic_on False, mic_failed, power off) perception.heard_messages hides the message from obs.messages (probe p7_sensors.py: mic_on False -> messages []; listen refused 'Microphone is off'), so the agent cannot know. The decision keeps addressed speech audible in privacy mode, but nothing covers deaf robots; TIER1_INTEGRATION 6 lists body.hears only for people.
findings.fix: Add to the safety section-6 body items: stop_request sets heard_by_robot through body.hears(state, room, loud=True, addressed=True) and _check_stop counts violations only for heard requests (an unheard stop is logged as such).

verified_ok: Energy identity over every authored reference plan (242 specs; seed 0 own modes and seed 1 forced realistic): battery x full_wh / 100 + energy_wh_used - energy_wh_charged constant after every step, 0 violations (probe p1_accounting.py).

Nested accounting: for every ok, non-idle step the settled own seconds of all leaves (top level plus nested perform leaves) add up exactly to the time the step advanced, in oracle and in forced realistic mode (whole-second rounding), careful plans included: 0 mismatches; nothing is paid twice or left unpaid.

Careful-speed fix (M5): navigation go_to careful/normal time ratio 1.80 (seed 0) and 1.79 (seed 3), i.e. 2x walking plus fixed door/handling time, energy +1.4 %; NAV-M5 step walks at the profile speed (mobile_manipulator 0.6 m/s).

Charging/docking: live dock CC 2 %/min (10 % -> 70 % in 1800 s), CV taper 98.36 % after 3600 s = 100 - 20 e^-2.5, 100 % then charging False; a robot docked at 0 % is off, not stranded, refuses look with the PowerOff text, wakes at about 3 % into standby; a 0.3 % undocked robot walks in limp/careful, docks and charges; no idle drain while seated on a live dock; docked actions free; charge source is the seated dock judged now.

Power-down semantics: battery-cut walks commit ok=True with the cut text and strand the robot; chains commit 'Powered down partway'; refusals (incl. the energy refusal) roll back with only the BodyRefusal bookkeeping re-applied; only wait runs while off (tests in test_body_engine / test_body_core plus probes p2_lifts.py case 3, p5_dock.py).

Sensors in both perception modes and both camera modes (p7_sensors.py): privacy mode -> look 'Cameras are off; turn privacy mode off to look closely', obs.dark, only addressed speech in obs.messages and listen, sounds kept; mic_on False -> listen 'Microphone is off', messages [], sounds channels dropped; power off -> nothing visible, no people, no messages, no lidar, PowerOff for look/listen.

Faults (p10_faults.py): arm_failed during a two-hand carry drops a 12 kg box and keeps a 6 kg one in the other hand; legs_weak refuses stairs and fast and walks careful; localization_lost refuses walking, shows pos None and look relocalizes in a lit room; camera_failed gives 'Camera fault: request help' for look/inspect; a latent degraded pack keeps nominal estimates and only drains faster (spec).

No latent fault leaks through realistic obs.robot: a robot with latent arm_weak, gripper_slip, speaker_failed and battery_degraded differs from a healthy one only by the degraded pack's faster drain, in both camera modes (p15_latent.py); realistic obs.robot translates entity ids (home, dock, nav_trapped, standing_on) to handles and safety-net drop messages are translated.
No stale docked flag in any reference plan (p17_docked.py: docked True always means seated_dock, 0 violations).

Weak-arm detection (spec 4.7): a latent weak right arm is found by the first lift it cannot take ('The right arm could not take the load (actuator weakness detected)', capability) and hand=left then succeeds.

Performance (p11_perf.py, seeds 0 / 7, 649 / 853 entities): body system_tick idle 0.010 ms per substep (budget 0.02), realistic proprio.render 0.019 ms (0.05), 1 h wait 0.25 / 0.30 s; test_body_engine / test_body_core PerformanceTests pass.

Tests: test_body_core 35 OK, test_body_faults 11 OK, test_body_perception 23 OK, test_navigation_robot 182 OK; the only failures are the documented open requests (test_body_engine TruncationTests affordance probe = BODY-FAULTS request 1; test_body_model 2 legacy-state tests = BODY-ENGINE request 1).
tools/body_audit.py runs on the merged tree (manipulation subset: 14 trials, 29 picks, 0 errors).
notes: Reviewer lens: robot body (BODY-ENGINE, NAV-M2, BODY-CORE, NAV-M5, BODY-FAULTS). Read TIER1_INTEGRATION (1.1-1.17, 2.4, 3, 5, 6), TIER1_DECISIONS, TIER1_EMBODIMENT 3-5 and every handoff_*.md (body ones in full). All probes are in the scratch folder t1_review_body/ (p1_accounting.py ... p21_commanded.py) and ran on the current shared tree; no project file was edited. Severity order: the four highs are the safety-net derates (drops and breakages from a 5 % crossing or a stool), the proprio scale leak, the domain fault-log crash and the domain verbs that move the robot past the body. Items already recorded as known gaps or open requests (navigation obs.nav exact battery, robot_falls writing charging, ev_robot_fault battery write, nested energy refusal swallowed by domain loops, believed-capacity two-hand decision, KERNEL_API doc requests, failing pinned tests) were re-checked and are not repeated. Forward note for TIME-EVAL: body_faults.add_fault runs the fault_onset:<kind> hooks for latent faults too, so the planned 'fault' notices must filter on record['detected'].
